statements.quote: Note that we pre-registered 200 responses per AI. However, slightly more responses were generated by our RAs, and we decided to include all of them in the analysis.

Note that the actual number of participants in each treatment group slightly di↵ers from the preregistered targets. We initially aimed for 700, 300, and 300 participants, recruited via Prolific. However, we received 702, 304, and 315 complete responses, respectively, due to the intentional invitation of a larger pool of participants to account for potential dropout before task completion.

We pre-registered two measures to evaluate the strategic skill: 

1. Frequency of suboptimal ’rock’ choices in the last 12 rounds. 

2. Points accumulated in the last 12 rounds.

deposits.notes: Paper names AEARCTR-0011584; the public record is titled Limits and capabilities of LLM and lists Bohren, Hakimov, and Lalive. Public HTML supplies the preregistered protocol, prompts, planned treatments, outcomes, and task instructions; it does not supply observed participant assignments, outcome values, or participant-produced texts. Materials-only refers to this public protocol text, not to downloadable attachments. No public file links appear in Supporting Documents and Materials, Analysis Plan, Program Files, or Reports, Papers & Other Materials; n_files=0 counts visible public attachments only. Under Data Publication the record explicitly says "Is public data available?" followed by "No". Last updated July 04, 2023; it still reports the study as In development, so this is not proof of present-day nonexistence elsewhere. The public citation DOI https://doi.org/10.1257/rct.11584-1.1 returned HTTP 200 and redirected to https://www.socialscienceregistry.org/trials/11584/history/185149. Some other registry sections show a generic notice that information is unavailable to the public and a Request Information button; no access was requested, and this does not establish a restricted participant-data deposit. Relevant to final.open_items 1 and 3, the public Interventions and Experimental Design sections state: "Later addition: In an additional treatment, we screen participants who have access to one of the AI LLM platforms, and encourage them to generate responses to the creative questions using AI. The strategic task remains unchanged." The record also gives Randomization Method as "based on randomization in qualtrics" and Randomization Unit as "participant". These are design clues; without participant data they do not resolve all recruitment or actual-use questions.

notes: Checked 2026-10-09 using Python urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1; no email address, personal identifier, login, account creation, access request, or bot-check bypass was used. Read all 97,819 characters of the saved markdown, including references and the complete appendix, and checked the PDF for availability/preregistration locators, links, and embedded files (40 pages; no embedded files). Quotes are exact excerpts from the saved markdown, retaining its ligature-conversion artifacts; locators refer to the saved IZA PDF, whose printed pagination is PDF page minus 2 after the front matter. There is no explicit data-on-request statement, code-availability statement, repository URL, or supplementary-material URL in the paper. The screening form data_and_code.data_url and code_url are both empty. The only relevant public external resource found is the AEA preregistration/protocol; no participant-level, output-level, or rating-level data file was found or read. Consequently no per-person means, arm SDs/SEs, standardized effects, analyzed counts, rater-condition estimates, attrition checks, Table 7 set sizes, or text-diversity statistics can be computed from located public data. This leaves the statistical parts of final.open_items 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, and 8 unresolved; item 9 is a codebook decision. The registry offers documentary evidence relevant to items 1 and 3, described in its deposit notes. Appendix Table 13 prints selected best/median texts with source, prompt, and creativity scores; it is not the full participant sample, has no participant identifier column, and cannot support the requested arm-level or diversity analyses. Printed tables, selected examples, and article mirrors are not counted as data deposits or as public_partial data. Link and publisher audit: https://www.iza.org (the paper's www.iza.org address) returned HTTP 500; https://www.iza.org/publications/dp/17302/creative-and-strategic-capabilities-of-generative-ai-evidence-from-large-scale-experiments and https://www.iza.org/publications/dp/17302 also returned HTTP 500. The publisher error page contained no article-specific supplementary-file links. https://docs.iza.org/dp17302.pdf returned HTTP 200, application/pdf, 1,853,423 bytes. The candidate DOI https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.4963992 redirected to https://www.ssrn.com/abstract=4963992 and returned HTTP 403 with a Just a moment bot-check page; stopped there. The only PDF-embedded external links are in the reference to the different Girotra et al. paper: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4526071 and http://dx.doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.4526071 (the latter appears twice). Both returned HTTP 403 at https://www.ssrn.com/abstract=4526071 with the same bot check; these are not c035 deposits. The candidate's EconStor lead https://www.econstor.eu/handle/10419/305744 returned HTTP 200 and lists only dp17302.pdf, with no supplementary data. Its file https://www.econstor.eu/bitstream/10419/305744/1/dp17302.pdf returned HTTP 200, 1,956,702 bytes, 41 pages including an added EconStor cover; opened in memory only. EconStor states all rights reserved unless otherwise indicated; no dataset license was identified. All four required repository services returned usable title and first-author search results after correcting Zenodo's unauthenticated page-size limit. HTTP failures and the unavailable publisher supplement listing limit confidence in an exhaustive negative finding. No GitHub repository was named, so no GitHub API calls were made.
